newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close on big gain, heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close on big gain, heavy volume.

text.p: French shares closed with a jump of more than one percent in heavy turnover, tracking the "Santa Claus rally" on Wall Street, traders said.

"The big push was today before people head for the hills, said a senior equity salesman, referring to departures for the Christmas week holiday. People also wanted to trade today as Monday marks the end of the December account.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 29.83 points or 1.33 percent at 2,278.53. The index was up 3.4 percent on the week. The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,280 from 2,250 on Thursday's close.
Volume was a massive 13.05 billion francs.
The linkage with New York worried some operators who felt the Paris market was rising too fast and Wall Street needed to consolidate. The Dow's recent volatility has also worried operators here.
But funds appeared to be underinvested and were looking to place money before the end of the year, to avoid tax payments, the senior equity salesman said.
If Wall Street continues its climb, investors will continue to seek high-quality stocks, a U.S. broker here said.
Meanwhile, pharmaceuticals and retailers sparkled.
* Bid speculation pushed the pharmaceuticals sector, including Sanofi, up 6.3 percent to 525 francs, Rhone-Poulenc up 5.84 percent to 177.5 and Synthelabo, up 0.91 percent to 554.

* Holders of Roussel Uclaf locked in profits by selling today, on the first day of the Hoechst buy-out, rather than wait for the January 24 close of the offer and waiting for cash settlement in February. The stock firmed 5.7 percent at 1,521. The offer was launched at 1,530 francs per share.
* Alcatel Alsthom weakens 2.1 percent to 416.7 francs, viewed a candidate for buying Thomson-CSF.
* Lagardere also bucks trend, ends down 0.63 percent at 142 francs. The government expects to announce plans for the Thomson-CSF sell-off early in the new year.
* Alcatel has significant upside potential at these levels, once the uncertainty over the Thomson sale is resolved, brokers said.
* Eurotunnel fell 1.43 percent to 6.90 francs. The volatile stock appeared to be damaged by Thursday's small fire at the Folkestone terminal which was quickly put out.
* Michelin ends off lows, but still down 0.15 percent at 273.10 francs.
* Michelin, another volatile stock partly due to lack of clear financial communications, has been dogged by rumours of a convertible bond and capital increase.
* Renault finishes with steep losses at 2.90 percent at 104.1 francs, considered the weaker of the two French carmakers and leass capable of facing the poor market outlook for 1997.

* Moulinex after the close posted a first-half 1996/96 net attributable loss of 74 million francs versus a 121 million loss a year ago. It also plans a 500 million franc capital increase early next year.
* Carrefour, favoured retailer among international funds, gains 1.68 percent to 3,332 francs.

* On the charts the next major resistance levels on the CAC index are 2,300 and 2,350, and the market could try to regain the historic high hit early in 1994 at 2,360.98. Other major centres have hit fresh record highs.

* The main lines of the merger between Dassault Aviation and Aerospatiale are due to be set early in the New Year, a defence ministry official said. Proposals for the industrial organisation have been sent to the government.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
